headword: {定年退職|ていねんたいしょく}
gloss: mandatory retirement; retirement at the set age

definitions.gloss: mandatory retirement; retirement at the prescribed age
definitions.explanation: Leaving one's employment upon reaching the company's or organization's mandatory retirement age. In Japan, this is typically 60 or 65 years old.

examples.japanese: {来年|らいねん}{定年退職|ていねんたいしょく}する。
examples.english: I will retire at mandatory age next year.

examples.japanese: {父|ちち}は{六十五歳|ろくじゅうごさい}で{定年退職|ていねんたいしょく}した。
{定年退職|ていねんたいしょく}{後|ご}は{趣味|しゅみ}の{旅行|りょこう}を{楽|たの}しみたいと{思|おも}っている。
examples.english: After mandatory retirement, I want to enjoy my hobby of traveling.

notes:
Compound noun: {定年|ていねん} (mandatory retirement age) + {退職|たいしょく} (resignation, leaving a job). Commonly used with する as a suru-verb.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {定年退職|ていねんたいしょく}する (to retire at mandatory age)
- {定年退職|ていねんたいしょく}{後|ご} (after mandatory retirement)
- {定年退職|ていねんたいしょく}を{迎|むか}える (to reach mandatory retirement)

CULTURE:
Japan's mandatory retirement age has been gradually raised. Many companies now offer {再雇用|さいこよう} (re-employment) programs allowing employees to continue working past the official retirement age, typically at reduced pay.
